content.text:
I've opened **[PR #397](https://github.com/cv/pit/pull/397)**. It says `Refs #396`, not `Closes`, and all 5 CI checks pass. It isn't merged or released yet, so the acceptance on a live pi-action thread is still to do; the PR lists those steps as a checklist.

## What changed
- **When it runs:** after every run that answers, including one that ended on a `terminate` round. The collapse goes into the same single `pit.context-edit` entry as the edits the model staged. The model's edits are recorded as before and the automatic ones as `operation: "collapse"`. A failed or aborted run collapses nothing and drops its staged edits, as before.
- **The line** looks like this:
  `[Pit: collapsed typescript call · "<label>" · workspace.read, workspace.search · ok · ~18.2K tokens · originals: session.inspectEntry("212"), session.inspectEntry("213")]`
  - The outcome is one of `ok`, `failed: <error's first line>`, `asked: <title>`, `saved <name>` or `no result`.
  - Other tools show their name and outcome.
  - An entry with several calls lists each one, separated by `;`.
- **What changes in the entry:** it keeps its text and thinking, signatures included. Its calls become the line and its results are omitted.
- **What it never touches:** user and host messages, answers, compaction summaries, notes, entries already rewritten or with a staged edit, entries no larger than their line, and the current run. If the model staged its own elide or summarize, the collapse skips those entries.
- **Compaction and forks:** it only reads the active context, so it never crosses the newest compaction head, and a fork keeps the view it had when it was taken.
- **Outline:** `session.outline()` shows collapsed entries as `elided`, with the line as the preview. I didn't add a new `collapsed` state, because the state type is part of the global contract shared with Pi.
- **Byte bound:** 512 bytes per line.
  - Labels and outcomes are cut to 160 characters each.
  - If the line is still too long, the injected functions go first, then the end of the description.
  - The token size and the `inspectEntry` IDs are never cut. When they don't fit, the IDs switch to a shorter form.
  - One exception: if an entry has so many parallel calls that its IDs alone pass 512 bytes, the line keeps all the IDs and names no calls.
- **Guideline:** when collapse is on, the durable guidelines gain the line you proposed: give each call a specific label, and say in the answer what a later run will need.

## Defaults (a behaviour change, listed in the changelog)
- **On by default**, with `collapse: { keepRuns: 1, minTokens: 32_000 }`. `collapse: false` turns it off.
- **`keepRuns: 1`** counts the run that just answered: it stays whole and older runs collapse.
- **`minTokens`** counts only the conversation's messages, not the system prompt, tools and sections. Those fixed parts are about 41K tokens on pi-action, so a floor on the whole context would always be passed. Below about 32K the transcript is smaller than the fixed prompt, so collapsing saves little; above that it dominates.

## Strict-provider check
I sent the collapsed shapes directly to Opus 5.5 through Anthropic's Messages API on NVIDIA's endpoint, the route pi-action uses, with adaptive thinking.
- **Accepted:**
  - user → two collapsed calls in a row, each keeping its real signed thinking → answer → follow-up, which is three assistant messages in a row;
  - the same without thinking;
  - a later run's live tool call and result after a collapsed run.

  So I kept the shape from the issue and didn't merge adjacent assistant messages.
- **With the guideline** in the system prompt, the model read the lines as its own earlier calls ("it called echo twice… both marked ok").
- **Without the guideline**, the model once said a collapsed line was "text I wrote myself", so the guideline matters.
- **Refused:** a request with the *same* signed thinking block sent twice, blocked as duplicating model output. That was an artificial copy I made for the probe. The collapse never copies a block, since each entry keeps its own.

`docs/durable.md` records these results.

## Tests
- **Real pi-durable harness:**
  - three runs with `keepRuns: 1`, where `inspectEntry` returns each original and a fork keeps its view;
  - nothing collapses when the conversation is under `minTokens` or with `collapse: false`;
  - a failed run (I added a `fail` option to the test harness);
  - a model elide in the same run, which lands in the same entry as the collapse;
  - a later run doesn't collapse anything twice.
- **Planning tests:** a table of line formats (the five cases you listed plus four more) and the byte bound.
- **`tests.probeMutation`:**
  - The `keepRuns` off-by-one was caught.
  - Making user and host messages stop starting a run was caught.
  - Treating answers as candidates was **not** caught. The collapse always keeps an entry's text, so an entry without calls can never get smaller and is never collapsed; answers stay protected even with that check removed.
- `delivery.validate` passes check, tests, coverage and the package check.
